title: Sprint Zero: hosting hypothesis, test plan, and exit criteria
body:
Purpose:
This is a short, pragmatic Sprint Zero doc to reduce risk for customer POCs that are undecided between hosted / dedicated / private hosting. The goal: run a 2–3 week lightweight validation that proves which hosting mode meets the customer's non-functional constraints and provides clear exit criteria for going to a longer pilot (dedicated reservation or private deployment).

Assumptions / context:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS with EU data residency requirements, ~200k monthly active inference calls (avg 80 tokens per call).
- Primary concerns: P50 latency < 120ms, 99.9% availability for plateau traffic, per-1k-token cost target (hosted) under $0.16, and end-to-end data isolation requirement for regulated endpoints.
- We have access to a representative sample prompt set and can replay traffic at low scale.

Sprint Zero hypothesis (what we will try to prove):
1) Hosted API will meet latency targets for baseline traffic and is the fastest path to value if data residency and contractual terms are acceptable.
2) Dedicated reserved capacity will show lower per-token cost at customer scale and better predictable tail latency under load.
3) Private (VPC/on-prem) will be required only if contractual data residency + KMS/HSM control requirements cannot be satisfied by hosted + dedicated offerings.

Scope of tests (2 weeks recommended):
- Week 1: smoke and functional parity checks (end-to-end request/response, auth, logging hooks).
- Week 1: latency profile sampling on hosted in target region (EU-west).
- Week 2: simulate production-like concurrency against a small dedicated pool (we can spin temporary dedicated nodes from lab capacity).
- Week 2: verify data path & encryption notes for private (demo ephemeral VPC) and confirm KMS integration feasibility.

Minimal test plan (concrete):
- Test 1 – Hosted latency sweep:
  - Replayer: 1 person runs traffic replayer with customer prompt sample (10k requests).
  - Measure: P50, P95, P99 latencies, time-to-first-byte, token throughput.
  - Pass if P50 <120ms and P95 <350ms and error rate <0.5%.

- Test 2 – Hosted cost projection:
  - Use sampled token distribution and Redwood cost sheet to extrapolate monthly cost at current traffic pattern.
  - Pass if estimated cost per 1k tokens <= $0.16 OR stakeholder OK with delta after negotiation.

- Test 3 – Dedicated stability under burst:
  - Provision small dedicated pool (2 GPUs equiv) for 48 hours from lab.
  - Replay scaled concurrency (x3 baseline).
  - Measure tail latency, queueing, and preemption behavior.
  - Pass if tail latency improves vs hosted (P95 down by >=20%) and throughput headroom exists.

- Test 4 – Data controls & private feasibility:
  - Smoke deploy an ephemeral private control-plane (demo package) in customer VPC or our lab air-gapped env.
  - Verify KMS key import/export, audit log path, and connectivity constraints.
  - Pass if no blocker in KMS integration or network policy; else document required infra work and time estimate.

Exit criteria (go/no-go decisions at end of Sprint Zero):
- Go Hosted -> pilot:
  - Hosted latency/cost tests pass AND legal OK with data residency/SLA AND customer prefers fastest time-to-market.
  - Next step: sign 3-month hosted pilot, enable per-route telemetry, and set up canary routing for failover.

- Go Dedicated -> pilot:
  - Hosted passes latency but cost projection exceeds target OR tail latency concerns persist under expected concurrency.
  - Next step: propose committed capacity size, expected unit price, and dedicated rollout plan (canary traffic splits).

- Go Private -> engineering evaluation required:
  - KMS / data sovereignty / contractual controls cannot be satisfied by hosted/dedicated within acceptable timeline or cost.
  - Next step: produce private deployment SOW, estimated infra cost, and 8–12 week delivery plan.

Decision matrix (quick summary):
- Hosted: fastest, lowest up-front friction, limited infra controls, good for MVP.
- Dedicated: predictable economics at scale, better tail behavior, requires commit and capacity ops.
- Private: maximal control, highest integration work and time-to-value.

Operational checklist during Sprint Zero (notes + owners):
- Provide customer telemetry template and data sample (Owner: Marco Chen).
- Create JIRA epic for pilot provisioning and link to this doc (Owner: Rita Gomez).
- Request legal to review data residency language (Owner: Samir Patel).
- Provision logging/tracing endpoint for customer validation (Owner: Alex Novak).

Lightweight measurements and gates (what to report back):
- Latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) for each hosting mode (artifact: CSV + grafana link).
- Cost model sheet with assumptions and sensitivity (artifact: spreadsheet link).
- Short risk register: items that would force private deployment and estimated mitigation time.

Communications plan:
- Daily 15m sync M-F during Sprint Zero in #solutions-pocs, summary notes posted to Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-ENG-5643).
- End-of-sprint stakeholder readout: 30m demo + decision runbook.

Open questions / TODOs (for immediate follow-up):
- Can Legal accept hosted data processing addendum with EU sub-processing clause? (TODO: Samir to escalate; Jira SE-1287)
summary: Sprint Zero template to validate hosted vs dedicated vs private for a customer POC with concrete tests, pass/fail gates, and recommended next steps. Lightweight, 2-week plan to produce clear decision and pilot SOWs.
